summary: Blameless postmortem covering a GPU OOM cascade triggered by a new autoscaler policy combined with a model rollout. Root cause: autoscaler burst policy + mis-estimated KV cache memory footprint for a new quantized model. Mitigations: immediate rollback of policy, guardrail added to KV cache allocation, improved pre-rollout perf test. Q3 roadmap reprioritized to focus on autoscaler improvements, forecasting, and additional runbook drills.
transcript:
Header: 2025-06-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 80m | Recording: Zoom | Location: #infra-sync

[00:00] Aisha (PM): OK, uh, thanks everyone for jumping on. We're doing a blameless postmortem for yesterday's GPU OOM cascade and then we have a quick sync on Q3 items. Marco, can you start with a sketch of what happened?

[00:21] Marco (SRE): Yeah, sure. So timeline first: around 10:42 UTC yesterday we started seeing elevated OOM events on a small subset of prod pods after the v2.3 autoscaler change. It was a combination of the new burst policy that allowed a fast warm-up and an under-accounted KV cache growth for quantized LLM instances. Memory jumped, eviction policies didn't keep up, and then we had a cascade as pods restarted and rejoined.

[00:46] Elena (Infra Eng): I want to add, the model we rolled had a slightly different KV cache pattern — we thought quantized weights would reduce RAM, but the KV cache semantics changed actual working set. The estimator in the rollout checklist missed the peak working set for 8k seqs.

[01:08] Tom (ML Eng): Right, there was one assumption in the mem-estimator that the cache per-token would be linear; for this variant it has a non-linear growth when the prefix cache hits certain thresholds. I flagged it in PR but it didn't block.

[01:31] Marco (SRE): Also, our autoscaler burst window allowed 3x scaling in under two minutes. That increased concurrency and multiplied the aggregate KV cache footprint. We should probably gate burst by memory headroom, not just GPU util.

[01:50] Aisha (PM): So immediate mitigations yesterday were?

[01:55] Marco (SRE): Rollback to autoscaler v2.2, manual cordon of affected nodes, restart with friendlier eviction policies. Also we disabled the new model rollout. That restored stability by ~11:10 UTC.

[02:15] Elena (Infra Eng): We also applied a short-term fix: cap per-session KV-cache allocation at 1.2x the predicted. It's a stopgap. Need a real guardrail in runtime.

[02:34] Priya (Product Ops): Did any customers see errors / latencies? I saw a spike in error rates on a couple of routes but it looks like automatic retries masked some of it.

[02:46] Tom (ML Eng): We saw elevated 5xxs on the hosted API for about 25 minutes. No major customer-facing outages but some tail latency spikes and elevated token error rates. We'll prepare a one-page incident note.

[03:09] Aisha (PM): OK, let's go through root cause at a high level: 1) rollout of a model variant with different KV characteristics; 2) autoscaler burst settings that scale without memory gating; 3) perf tests that didn't exercise the non-linear working set. Anything else?

[03:33] Marco (SRE): Small infra detail: the node-level oom_killer behavior is noisy; we should tune oom_score_adj for inference containers so endpoints with graceful shutdowns are favored.

[03:48] Elena (Infra Eng): And our rollout checklist missed a preflight simulation using the exact serving stack on k8s with 8k seqs. We had a synthetic test, but it used a different kv-cache mode.

[04:06] Aisha (PM): Sounds like action items around autoscaler, KV cache guardrails, perf tests, and runbooks. Let's capture all those.

[04:22] Marco (SRE): For autoscaler: immediate rollback (done), short-term change: add memory-headroom gating. Long-term: implement a cost model that estimates per-pod memory given model variant and concurrent sessions.

[04:46] Tom (ML Eng): For perf tests, I propose a new 'rollout-sim' harness that spins up a small cluster with the exact runtime and runs multi-session traces with configured sequence lengths. It should run as part of the deployment pipeline.

[05:10] Elena (Infra Eng): I'll own the KV-cache guardrail — adding an allocation cap plus an early-fail mode that rejects sessions that would exceed safe memory. We need a telemetry signal for when the guardrail trips.

[05:31] Priya (Product Ops): From a product ops standpoint I'll draft the incident summary and decide whether to notify customers; I think an internal blameless note plus a brief customer note is sufficient unless execs want more.

[05:50] Aisha (PM): Good. Now quick Q3 roadmap implications — I suggested elevating autoscaler and rollout safety to R1. We may delay one feature to make room. Thoughts?

[06:12] Tom (ML Eng): Agree. We should pause the big LRU-memory optimization effort and focus resources on safety and quantized-model profiling. The customer benefit is less risky if we ensure reliability.

[06:31] Marco (SRE): Also need more on-call drills; yesterday felt disorganized between SRE and infra during the cascade. We should schedule runbooks and tabletop drills.

[06:47] Elena (Infra Eng): We should also budget for additional monitoring: per-pod kv-cache histograms and ephemeral memory breakdowns. It's a small capex for observability but high ROI.

[07:05] Aisha (PM): Priya, can you update the roadmap doc after this call and propose which feature we push to Q4?

[07:14] Priya (Product Ops): Yep, I'll do that — propose pushing the LRU opt and pull forward autoscaler hardening and rollout-sim.

[07:26] Tom (ML Eng): Quick note on testing: we need to add a preflight step that uses model-variant metadata (kv-cache multiplier) to compute expected working set. That metadata needs to be stored with the model in the catalog.

[07:48] Marco (SRE): Agreed. Also, immediate config: set autoscaler burst to 1.25x and cap concurrent warm-ups per node. We'll monitor for the week.

[08:01] Elena (Infra Eng): For the longer guardrail, I want to propose a lightweight admission controller that reads model annotations and denies pods that would exceed node headroom. Might be medium effort but avoids another rollout causing OOMs.

[08:20] Aisha (PM): OK, let's surface priorities for PR/engineer assignment. Marco on autoscaler short-term rollback (done) + gating (owner: Marco). Elena on guardrail + admission controller. Tom on rollout-sim and model metadata. Priya on comms. I'll own roadmap reprioritization.

[08:42] Marco (SRE): I'll open the autoscaler PR today and target the gating change for a hotfix by 6/19.

[08:50] Tom (ML Eng): I'll prototype the rollout-sim in a fork and run initial runs by EOW. We should add a checklist item to block rollouts without successful sim runs.

[09:04] Elena (Infra Eng): I'll sketch the admission controller design and a phased rollout: 1) runtime guardrail; 2) admission controller; 3) admission webhook integration.

[09:21] Priya (Product Ops): For comms, do we want a customer-facing note? If so, I can draft a short message: "We experienced elevated 5xxs; root cause identified and mitigations applied; no data loss, resiliency improvements planned."

[09:41] Aisha (PM): Yeah, prepare the note but hold off until we sync with legal/ops, keep it concise and factual.

[09:57] Marco (SRE): One more operational ask: add an SLO alert specifically for aggregate KV-cache growth across namespace — that could warn us early.

[10:12] Elena (Infra Eng): We'll add histograms and alert with a 10-minute lookback and 3-sigma threshold.

[10:26] Tom (ML Eng): Another thing — our quantization docs need a section on KV semantics so engineers adding model variants know to test cache behavior. I'll add a PR to docs.

[10:44] Aisha (PM): Great. Any blockers?

[10:47] Marco (SRE): I need access to the model catalog write perms to add metadata; Elena will help if needed.

[10:52] Elena (Infra Eng): I'll provision a group to allow model owners to tag kv-cache multipliers.

[11:01] Priya (Product Ops): I'll schedule a tabletop drill next week, invite SRE and Infra and at least one on-call.

[11:18] Aisha (PM): OK let's recap and close. Recap: rollback done; autoscaler gating hotfix by 6/19; KV-cache guardrail + admission plan owned by Elena; rollout-sim owned by Tom; docs + model metadata; runbook drills scheduled by Priya; roadmap re-prioritized by Aisha. Action owners and due dates shared in next steps.

[11:46] Marco (SRE): Quick log note: please link monitoring dashboards and the metric ids in the incident doc.

[11:58] Priya (Product Ops): Will do.

[12:05] Aisha (PM): Thanks everyone. Any final thoughts?

[12:12] Tom (ML Eng): Just that we should add a small staging canary that exercises large sequence lengths during rollouts; catches this earlier.

[12:21] Elena (Infra Eng): Agree.

[12:26] Aisha (PM): Cool, meeting adjourned. I'll publish the blameless note after PRs land.
